title: Why Lenexa Families Choose Meylor Chiropractic & Acupuncture
excerpt: Discover why Lenexa families choose Meylor Chiropractic & Acupuncture. Dr. Jade Meylor offers holistic, root-cause care for all ages across Johnson County.
content:
Choosing a chiropractor is a personal decision. You are not just looking for someone to relieve a sore back. You are looking for a partner in your family's health, someone who listens, understands your goals, and treats you like a person rather than a number. For families across Lenexa and Johnson County, that search often ends at Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture.

Led by Dr. Jade Meylor, our Lenexa practice has earned the trust of hundreds of local families since 2005 through a unique blend of advanced diagnostic technology, holistic philosophy, and genuine personal care. This article shares what sets us apart, the kinds of transformations patients experience, and why so many people across Lenexa, Olathe, and Overland Park have made us their family chiropractor.

## More Than Pain Relief: A Holistic Philosophy

Most people first visit a chiropractor because something hurts. Back pain, neck stiffness, headaches, or an old injury that will not quit. While Dr. Meylor absolutely helps patients find relief from these issues, what makes our Lenexa office different is the philosophy behind the care.

Rather than simply chasing symptoms, Dr. Meylor focuses on the root cause. Why is your body struggling? What is interfering with its natural ability to heal? This whole-body, root-cause approach is the foundation of everything we do. According to the [American Chiropractic Association](https://www.acatoday.org/), this kind of patient-centered, conservative care plays an important role in overall health and wellness.

When you address the underlying cause instead of masking the symptom, two things happen. First, you get longer-lasting relief. Second, you often notice improvements in areas you did not even come in for, like better sleep, more energy, and fewer headaches. To see the full range of issues we help with, visit our [chiropractic care services](/services/chiropractic/) page.

This is the difference between feeling patched up and feeling truly well. It is the reason so many Lenexa families stay with us long after their initial concern is resolved.

## What Sets Dr. Meylor Apart

There are many chiropractors across Johnson County, so what makes Dr. Meylor the choice for so many local families? It comes down to a rare combination of advanced training, gentle technique, and a genuine commitment to whole-family care.

## Advanced Diagnostic Technology

Dr. Meylor uses modern diagnostic tools to identify the exact source of dysfunction before treatment ever begins. Rather than guessing, we measure. This precision is what allows our adjustments to be both effective and gentle, and it means your care plan is built around your specific findings rather than a one-size-fits-all protocol.

## Titleist Performance Institute Certification

Dr. Meylor is one of the few chiropractors in the Kansas City area with [Titleist Performance Institute certification](/services/golf/), making her the go-to provider for golfers seeking to recover from injury and improve performance on the course.

## Prenatal and Pediatric Expertise

Pregnancy changes the body in profound ways, and the right chiropractic care can make a meaningful difference in comfort and function. Our [pregnancy chiropractic care](/services/chiropractic/family-chiropractic/pregnancy/) supports moms through every trimester, and our [family and pediatric care](/services/chiropractic/family-chiropractic/) brings that same gentle approach to children of every age.

## Acupuncture Under the Same Roof

Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture also offers traditional [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/), giving Lenexa patients another effective pathway to relief from pain, stress, sinus issues, and more — all coordinated with your chiropractic plan.

## Whole-Family Care Under One Roof

One of the things Lenexa families appreciate most is that Meylor Chiropractic truly serves everyone. You do not need a different provider for each member of your family. Dr. Meylor cares for:

- Infants and toddlers with gentle techniques for issues like colic, reflux, and sleep
- Children and teens for posture, sports performance, and healthy development
- Pregnant moms for comfort, balance, and a smoother delivery
- Working adults for back pain, neck pain, headaches, and stress
- Active aging adults and seniors for mobility, joint health, and vitality

When your whole family sees the same trusted provider, Dr. Meylor gets to know your family's unique health patterns and goals. For more on what this looks like in practice, see our guide to [family chiropractic care in Lenexa](/patients/blog/finding-headache-migraine-relief-meylor/) and our overview of [pregnancy and postpartum chiropractic care](/patients/blog/pregnancy-postpartum-care-safe-chiropractic/).

## Transformation Across Conditions and Life Stages

Every patient who walks through our doors in Lenexa has a different story, but the common thread is transformation. New moms often arrive during pregnancy seeking relief from lower back and pelvic discomfort, then return after birth to bring in their newborns for gentle care. Working professionals who came in for chronic neck pain frequently discover that their headaches and poor sleep improve as well. Active adults and weekend athletes use regular care to recover faster and stay in the game. Seniors find that consistent, gentle adjustments help them maintain the mobility and independence they value most.

These transformations happen because Dr. Meylor treats the whole person, not just the complaint. Research summarized by the [National Institutes of Health](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/spinal-manipulation-what-you-need-to-know) continues to support the value of conservative, hands-on care for many of the most common musculoskeletal conditions.

## Trusted by Johnson County: 400+ Five-Star Reviews

Reputation matters, especially when it comes to your family's health. Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture has earned more than 400 five-star reviews from patients across Lenexa, Olathe, Overland Park, Shawnee, and the wider Johnson County area, and was voted [Best of 2026](/about/team/) by the local community.

These reviews reflect what we hear in the office every day: patients feel genuinely listened to, Dr. Meylor takes the time to explain what is happening and why, and the care they receive makes a real difference in their daily lives. When you are searching for the best chiropractor in Lenexa, the experiences of your neighbors are one of the most reliable guides you will find.

## A Modern Office with a Personal Touch

Walking into Meylor Chiropractic, you will notice the difference right away. Our Lenexa office combines modern chiropractic methods with a warm, welcoming atmosphere where you are treated like family, not a number on a chart.

Here is what you can expect:

title: Back Pain After Gardening and Yard Work
excerpt: Back pain after yard work in Lenexa? Same-day chiropractic care for gardening injuries, lifting strain, and weekend flare-ups. Call (913) 227-0909.
content:
The weekend started so well. A clear Kansas morning, a long list of yard projects, and the satisfaction of finally tackling the flower beds, the mulch pile, and the back patio all in one Saturday. Then Sunday morning hits, and you cannot bend over to tie your shoes. Your lower back is locked up, every movement sends a sharp twinge through your hips, and the rest of the weekend is suddenly off the table.

This pattern is so common in Lenexa that we see a noticeable spike in acute back pain visits every spring and summer. Yard work is one of the most physically demanding things many homeowners do all year, yet most people approach it like it is a casual chore. At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, we help patients get out of acute flare-ups quickly and back to enjoying their summer. This guide explains why gardening hurts so many backs, what to do when it happens to you, and how to prevent the next round.

## Why Gardening and Yard Work Trigger So Many Back Injuries

Lawn care and gardening combine almost every movement that puts the lumbar spine at risk: repetitive bending, twisting under load, prolonged kneeling, and lifting things that are heavier than they look. According to ergonomics guidance from the [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/topics/ergonomics/), this combination of awkward postures and sustained loading is a leading driver of musculoskeletal injuries across virtually every population group.

For Lenexa homeowners, the specific culprits we see again and again include:

- **Repetitive bending without bending the knees.** Pulling weeds, planting flowers, and edging beds all invite folding from the waist instead of squatting properly.

- **Twisting while lifting.** Picking up a bag of mulch and turning to dump it is the single most common mechanism of acute disc injury we see.

- **Prolonged kneeling.** Long stretches in one position lock the hips and lower back into a flexed pattern.

- **Overestimating bag weights.** A wet bag of soil or mulch can weigh significantly more than the label suggests.

- **Power tool use.** The vibration and awkward postures involved in trimmers, mowers, and edgers create cumulative strain over hours.

- **Sudden weekend warrior effort.** Sitting at a desk all week, then attempting six straight hours of intense yard work, is a recipe for injury.

These mechanisms commonly trigger conditions we treat regularly, including acute [lower back pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/back-pain/), [sciatica](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/sciatica/), and [disc injuries](/services/chiropractic/injuries/disc-injury/).

## What's Actually Happening When Your Back Locks Up

That sudden, sharp pain after yard work is rarely random. It is usually one of a few specific things happening in your lower back.

## Lumbar Muscle Strain

The most common scenario. Overworked muscles in the lower back develop micro-tears, then go into protective spasm. The result is intense stiffness and pain that limits motion in every direction. Muscle strain typically improves with proper care over several days to a few weeks.

## Facet Joint Irritation

The small joints at the back of your spine can become inflamed and irritated from repetitive bending and twisting. This often shows up as sharp, localized pain on one side of the lower back that worsens with extension or rotation.

## Disc Bulge or Herniation

If the pain radiates down a leg, includes numbness or tingling, or feels sharp and electric, you may have aggravated a spinal disc. The combination of bending forward, lifting, and twisting is the classic mechanism for disc injuries. These cases respond well to early conservative care but are easy to make worse if mishandled.

## Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction

The sacroiliac (SI) joints connect your spine to your pelvis. Repeated asymmetrical loading from yard work can throw these joints out of alignment, creating deep, one-sided pain in the lower back and buttock that often gets blamed on the lumbar spine when the real source is the SI joint.

Sorting out which of these is driving your pain matters because each responds to slightly different care. This is exactly what your evaluation covers when you come in.

## Same-Day and Urgent Care Availability at Our Lenexa Office

One of the most frustrating parts of an acute back injury is the wait. You hurt your back on Saturday, your primary care office is closed on Sunday, and the soonest opening is two weeks out. Meanwhile, every hour you spend braced in protective tension makes the muscles tighter and the recovery slower.

Same-day appointments are often available at our Lenexa office. If you wake up Monday morning unable to move after a weekend of yard work, call us first thing. Acute back pain responds dramatically better to early care than to days of rest and ice that allow the protective spasm pattern to dig in. For more on this approach, see our guide to [emergency chiropractic care in Lenexa](/patients/blog/emergency-chiropractic-care-lenexa-same-day-relief-acute-back-pain/).

For severe cases or if your pain stems from a recent auto incident on top of physical strain, our [auto injury relief care](/services/auto-injury-relief/) includes specific protocols for layered trauma.

## What to Do in the First 24 to 48 Hours

While you wait to be seen, a few smart moves can keep the situation from getting worse:

- **Move gently and often.** Complete bed rest actually slows recovery. Short, easy walks every hour help reduce protective spasm.

- **Apply ice for the first 24 hours.** Twenty minutes on, then off for at least an hour. Ice helps with acute inflammation.

- **Switch to heat after the first day.** Once acute swelling has settled, heat helps relax tight muscles.

- **Avoid bending and twisting.** Especially together. Squat to pick things up and pivot with your feet rather than turning at the waist.

- **Hydrate.** Dehydrated discs and muscles recover more slowly.

- **Skip the heavy painkillers if possible.** Masking pain can lead to movements that worsen the injury. Discuss medication with your doctor if needed.

- **Call us early.** The first 48 hours are the most important window for fast recovery.

## How Chiropractic Care Speeds Recovery From Yard Work Injuries

Chiropractic care is particularly well-suited to acute back flare-ups because it addresses the specific mechanical issues that yard work creates. Your visit typically includes:

- **Targeted spinal adjustments.** Restoring motion to restricted joints relieves pressure and breaks the protective spasm cycle.

- **Soft tissue therapy.** Releasing tight muscles surrounding the injury speeds healing and reduces compensatory tightness.

- **Flexion-distraction.** Gentle, rhythmic spinal decompression that is especially effective for disc-related strain.

- **Acupuncture.** For stubborn inflammation and chronic flare-up patterns, our [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/) add another effective layer of relief.

- **Corrective stretches and exercises.** Specific movements that restore mobility and prevent re-injury.

This approach is part of our broader [chiropractic care services](/services/chiropractic/), which focus on whole-body recovery rather than just symptom suppression.

## Prevention Tips for Lenexa Homeowners

Once your acute pain is resolved, the goal shifts to preventing the next one. Back pain prevention guidance from the [National Institutes of Health](https://www.niams.nih.gov/health-topics/back-pain) consistently points to the same fundamentals: proper lifting mechanics, regular movement, and core strength. A few smart habits make a meaningful difference for any Lenexa homeowner heading into a busy yard work season:

- **Warm up first.** Five minutes of brisk walking and gentle stretching before grabbing the shovel.

- **Use the right tools.** Long-handled tools reduce bending, kneeling pads protect your hips, and wheelbarrows save your spine.

- **Lift with your legs.** Squat down, keep the load close to your body, and never twist mid-lift.

- **Break up the workload.** Two shorter sessions over a weekend are easier on your back than one marathon day.

- **Change positions often.** Switch between standing, kneeling, and squatting every 15 to 20 minutes.

- **Stay hydrated and take breaks.** Kansas heat amplifies fatigue, and fatigue is when injuries happen.

- **Strengthen your core year-round.** A strong midsection is the best back insurance.

If neck and shoulder tightness also flare during yard work, especially from looking down at garden beds or wielding power tools, the same approach we use for [neck pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/neck-pain/) applies.

## Get Same-Day Relief From Yard Work Back Pain

You do not have to spend the rest of summer on the couch. We offer free consultations and same-day appointments, so you can get treated quickly and back to enjoying your home and the season. Acute back pain responds best to early care.

Schedule Free Consultation Call (913) 227-0909

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How quickly can I be seen after a weekend yard work injury?**

Same-day appointments are often available, especially Monday mornings when many patients call after a weekend flare-up. Call us at (913) 227-0909 as early as possible to secure a spot.

**Should I see a chiropractor or my regular doctor first?**

For acute musculoskeletal back pain without red-flag symptoms like loss of bladder control, severe weakness, or numbness in the groin area, chiropractic care is often the most direct path to relief. We will refer you to your physician or to imaging if anything in your evaluation suggests it is needed.

**How many visits will I need?**

Most acute yard work injuries respond well within three to six visits. More severe strains or disc-related issues may require several weeks of consistent care. Dr. Meylor will outline a specific plan after your first evaluation.

**Is it safe to keep gardening while I am being treated?**

Light activity is usually fine and often helpful. Heavy lifting, twisting, and prolonged bending should be paused until your symptoms have improved. We will give you specific guidelines based on your situation.

**Can chiropractic help if my pain is radiating down my leg?**

Yes. Sciatica and disc-related leg pain respond well to conservative chiropractic care, especially when addressed early. Techniques like flexion-distraction are particularly effective for these patterns.

**Will insurance cover treatment for a yard work injury?**

Most insurance plans cover chiropractic care for acute back pain and related conditions. Call (913) 227-0909 to verify your specific coverage before your first visit.

## Visit Our Lenexa Chiropractic Office

Our office is conveniently located at 12980 W 87th St Pkwy in Lenexa, easy to reach from Overland Park, Shawnee, Olathe, and surrounding Johnson County communities. We prioritize same-day availability for acute back pain whenever possible because we know summer waits for no one.

title: Stress and Tension Relief Through Chiropractic Care in Lenexa: Your Body Keeps the Score
excerpt: Stress relief chiropractor in Lenexa eases tension headaches, neck tightness, and jaw pain. Reset your body with regular care. Call (913) 227-0909.
content:
Stress does not just live in your head. It settles into your shoulders, clenches your jaw, tightens your lower back, and tenses every muscle you cannot consciously relax. For the busy professionals, working parents, and high-performing students across Lenexa, that physical weight builds quietly over weeks and months until it becomes the headache that will not go away, the neck pain that lingers all weekend, or the back tightness that no amount of stretching seems to fix.

The phrase "your body keeps the score" captures this reality perfectly. Stress is not something you simply think your way out of, because by the time it reaches the muscles and joints, it is no longer a thought. It is a physical pattern. At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, we help people across Lenexa interrupt that pattern, release the tension stored in their bodies, and create the kind of regular reset that modern life rarely allows for.

## How Chronic Stress Shows Up in the Body

When you experience stress, your nervous system shifts into what is commonly called fight-or-flight mode. Your heart rate climbs, your breathing becomes shallow, and your muscles tense in preparation for action. This response is meant to be short-lived. In the modern world, it rarely is.

The result is a body stuck in low-grade tension day after day. According to research from the [American Psychological Association](https://www.apa.org/topics/stress/body), chronic stress is directly linked to musculoskeletal pain, persistent headaches, jaw clenching, gastrointestinal issues, and disrupted sleep. The physical toll is real and measurable.

For our patients in Lenexa, the most common physical signs of unresolved stress include:

- **Tension headaches.** Often felt as a tight band around the head or a deep ache at the base of the skull.

- **Neck and shoulder tightness.** Especially the upper trapezius muscles, which seem to permanently brace under stress.

- **Jaw pain and clenching.** Frequently worse at night, sometimes waking you with a sore jaw or headache.

- **Upper back tightness between the shoulder blades.** The classic "knot" that returns no matter how much you stretch.

- **Lower back stiffness.** Especially common in people who sit through long, stressful workdays.

- **Shallow breathing and tight chest muscles.** Often unnoticed until someone points it out.

- **Disrupted sleep and difficulty fully relaxing.**

If any of these sound familiar, you are not alone, and there is a path forward.

## The Stress and Jaw Connection

One of the clearest examples of stress living in the body is jaw tension. Many of the patients we see in Lenexa do not realize how much they clench their teeth, particularly at night, until they wake up with a sore jaw, sensitive teeth, or a headache that started before they did. Jaw tension also commonly radiates into the neck and upper back, creating a feedback loop where the jaw pulls on the neck and the tight neck keeps the jaw clenched.

Chiropractic care addresses both ends of this loop. Adjustments to the upper cervical spine and soft tissue work around the jaw and surrounding muscles help reset the pattern. Our work on [neck pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/neck-pain/) is a natural extension of broader stress and tension care, and the two are almost always treated together.

If your headaches are part of this picture, our specific work on [headaches and migraines](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/headaches-migraines/) may also be relevant.

**"The body remembers what the mind tries to ignore. Tension stored in the muscles for weeks or months becomes part of how you stand, breathe, and even sleep."**

## Why Chiropractic Care Helps With Stress-Related Tension

Chiropractic care is most often associated with back and neck pain, but its effect on the nervous system makes it a powerful tool for stress-related tension. Here is what happens during care that directly counters chronic stress patterns.

## Activating the Parasympathetic Nervous System

Your autonomic nervous system has two branches: sympathetic (fight-or-flight) and parasympathetic (rest-and-digest). Chronic stress keeps the sympathetic branch dominant. Spinal adjustments, particularly to the upper cervical spine, have been shown to influence parasympathetic activation, helping the body shift back toward a calmer baseline. A review indexed by the [National Center for Biotechnology Information](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6597274/) documents these autonomic effects in clinical chiropractic care.

## Releasing Muscular Holding Patterns

Tight muscles do not loosen on their own once a holding pattern is established. Targeted soft tissue work and adjustments interrupt these patterns at the source, letting the muscles return to their normal resting tone. Many of our patients report a wave of relaxation that lasts well beyond the visit itself.

## Improving Sleep and Recovery

Sleep is the body's primary recovery window, and stress directly disrupts it. By reducing the physical tension that keeps people tossing and turning, chiropractic care often improves sleep quality, which in turn lowers stress in a positive cycle. We explored this loop in detail in our guide to [stress, sleep, and spinal health](/patients/blog/stress-sleep-spinal-health-interconnection/).

## Supporting Better Breathing

Stress drives shallow chest breathing, which keeps the nervous system on alert. Adjustments to the upper back and ribs, combined with soft tissue work, open the chest and restore the ability to breathe deeply, which signals safety to the nervous system.

This whole-body, whole-nervous-system approach is at the core of our broader [chiropractic care services](/services/chiropractic/).

## A Regular Reset for Lenexa's Busy Professionals and Families

One of the most important shifts to make is from thinking of chiropractic as something you do when pain becomes unbearable, to thinking of it as a regular reset that keeps you from getting there in the first place. The patients we see for stress-related tension consistently say the same thing: regular care helps them stay ahead of the buildup.

For working professionals juggling deadlines, parents shuttling kids to practices and games, and anyone caring for aging family members, chiropractic care provides a built-in pause. It is one of the few appointments in a busy week that exists solely to help your body let go. If you have been feeling the cumulative weight of a hard year, our reflection on [chiropractic care through the holidays](/patients/blog/chiropractic-care-through-holidays-staying-consistent/) speaks to why consistency matters most when life is loudest.

Many of our patients in Lenexa also combine chiropractic with [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/), which add another deeply calming layer to stress relief. The two modalities pair well for patients dealing with chronic tension, anxiety-related muscle holding, or stress-driven headaches.

## Practical Stress Management to Pair With Chiropractic Care

In-office care delivers the strongest results when paired with daily habits that keep the nervous system regulated. Here are simple strategies we often recommend:

- **Box breathing.** Inhale for four counts, hold for four, exhale for four, hold for four. Three minutes resets the nervous system.

- **Daily movement breaks.** Brief walks, especially outdoors, are remarkably effective at lowering stress hormones.

- **Limit doom scrolling.** Especially before bed. Cortisol-spiking content is not the friend of a tense body.

- **Magnesium-rich foods.** Leafy greens, nuts, and seeds support muscle relaxation naturally.

- **Consistent sleep schedule.** Same bedtime, same wake time, even on weekends.

- **Stretch the chest and hips.** The two areas that tighten most under desk-based stress.

If your stress patterns trace back to a previous injury that has not fully resolved, our [auto injury relief](/services/auto-injury-relief/) care can address those lingering physical contributors as well. And if you spend long hours at a desk, our guide to [posture correction and tech neck](/patients/blog/posture-correction-tech-neck-lenexa/) pairs naturally with stress care.

## Give Your Body the Reset It Needs

You do not have to keep carrying weeks of tension in your shoulders, jaw, and back. We offer [free consultations](/free-consultation/) and same-day appointments, so you can step into our office and start releasing the stress your body has been holding onto for far too long.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Stress Relief Chiropractic Care in Lenexa

**Can chiropractic care really help with stress?**

Yes. While chiropractic care does not address the emotional or psychological sources of stress, it directly relieves the physical tension stress creates. For many people, releasing that physical layer makes the mental and emotional load feel much more manageable.

**How often should I come in for stress and tension relief?**

It varies based on how much tension has built up and how reactive your nervous system is. Many patients start with weekly visits for a few weeks, then move to biweekly or monthly maintenance care to stay ahead of buildup.

**What if my stress is coming from work or family demands I cannot change?**

That is the case for most patients we see. The point of regular care is not to eliminate stress from your life. It is to keep the physical impact of that stress from accumulating into chronic pain, headaches, and dysfunction.

**Is chiropractic safe if I am dealing with anxiety?**

Yes. Chiropractic adjustments often have a calming effect on the nervous system, which many anxiety sufferers find helpful. We always tailor techniques to your comfort level and never use force that feels jarring.

**Do you treat children for stress-related tension?**

Yes. Stress affects kids too, particularly students dealing with academic pressure. Our gentle [pediatric techniques](/services/chiropractic/family-chiropractic/chiropractic-care-for-kids/) are well-suited for younger patients showing signs of tension headaches or chronic muscle tightness.

**Will my insurance cover stress-related chiropractic visits?**

Most insurance plans cover chiropractic care when there is a related musculoskeletal diagnosis like tension headaches, neck pain, or back tightness. Call us at (913) 227-0909 to confirm your specific coverage.

## Visit Our Lenexa Chiropractic Office

Our office is conveniently located at 12980 W 87th St Pkwy in [Lenexa](/lenexa/), easy to reach from Overland Park, Shawnee, Olathe, and surrounding Johnson County communities. Same-day appointments are often available when you need a stress reset that cannot wait for next week.

title: Numbness and Tingling in Hands and Feet: Chiropractic Solutions in Lenexa
excerpt: Numbness and tingling chiropractor in Lenexa treats nerve pain in hands and feet. Relief from pinched nerves and radiating pain. Call (913) 227-0909.
content:
That strange pins and needles feeling in your fingers. The foot that keeps going numb when you sit too long. A burning sensation that travels down your arm or leg for no obvious reason. These symptoms can be alarming, and for good reason. They are your nervous system telling you something is wrong. For many adults in Lenexa, numbness and tingling become daily companions long before they realize what is driving them.

The encouraging news is that most cases trace back to nerve compression in the spine, and that is something [chiropractic care](/services/chiropractic/) addresses directly. At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, we help patients identify the real source of their nerve symptoms and provide targeted care that relieves pressure on the affected nerves. This guide explains what causes numbness and tingling, how to tell different conditions apart, and when chiropractic care is the right next step.

## What Causes Numbness and Tingling in the Hands and Feet?

Numbness and tingling, medically known as paresthesia, occur when a nerve is irritated, compressed, or not receiving proper signals. According to the [National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/paresthesia), paresthesia affects millions of Americans and has dozens of potential causes, from pinched nerves to systemic conditions.

The most common sources of nerve symptoms we see at our Lenexa office include:

- **Cervical spine misalignment.** When vertebrae in the neck shift or restrict, they can compress the nerves that travel down into the shoulders, arms, and hands.

- **Lumbar spine compression.** Misalignment, disc bulges, or stenosis in the lower back compress the nerves that supply the legs and feet.

- **Carpal tunnel syndrome.** Compression of the median nerve at the wrist, often linked to repetitive motion and forward shoulder posture.

- **Thoracic outlet syndrome.** Compression of nerves and blood vessels between the collarbone and first rib.

- **Peripheral neuropathy.** Nerve damage from diabetes, vitamin deficiencies, certain medications, or other systemic causes.

Pinpointing which of these is actually driving your symptoms is the most important step toward real relief. Treating carpal tunnel when the problem is actually in the neck, or chasing foot numbness without checking the lower back, is exactly why so many people cycle through years of frustration without progress. Many of these patterns overlap with the postural issues we covered in our guide to [posture correction and tech neck in Lenexa](/patients/blog/posture-correction-tech-neck-lenexa/).

## How Spinal Misalignment Creates Numbness and Radiating Pain

To understand why chiropractic care helps so often with nerve symptoms, it helps to picture the spine as a protective tunnel. Your spinal cord runs through it, and at every level, pairs of nerve roots branch out through small openings between the vertebrae. Those nerves then travel to every part of your body, including the hands and feet.

When a vertebra shifts even slightly, a disc bulges, or surrounding tissues become inflamed, the small openings narrow. The nerves passing through them get irritated or compressed. The result is the classic pattern we see daily at our clinic: pain, numbness, or tingling that radiates along the path of the affected nerve.

## Symptoms That Often Trace Back to the Cervical Spine

Nerves exiting the neck supply the shoulders, arms, and hands. Compression here often shows up as:

- Tingling or numbness in specific fingers (the pattern points to specific nerves)

- A burning or electric sensation down the arm

- Weakness or clumsiness when gripping objects

- Shoulder pain that travels into the upper arm

- Headaches that accompany the arm symptoms

Our team frequently treats these patterns alongside chronic [neck pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/neck-pain/), since the same alignment issues usually drive both.

## Symptoms That Often Trace Back to the Lumbar Spine

Nerves from the lower back supply the legs and feet. Compression in this region often shows up as:

- Tingling or numbness down the back or side of the leg

- A deep aching or burning that runs from the buttock to the foot

- Weakness in the foot or difficulty lifting the toes

- Numbness in specific toes or along the outside of the foot

- Symptoms that worsen with prolonged sitting or standing

This pattern is most commonly associated with [sciatica](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/sciatica/) and related [disc injuries](/services/chiropractic/injuries/disc-injury/), both of which respond well to conservative chiropractic care when caught early.

## Carpal Tunnel vs. Sciatica vs. Peripheral Neuropathy: How to Tell the Difference

One of the most common questions we hear in Lenexa is some version of "How do I know what kind of nerve problem I have?" The symptoms can feel similar, but the underlying conditions are different and respond to different approaches.

## Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

Carpal tunnel involves compression of the median nerve at the wrist. Classic signs include numbness or tingling in the thumb, index, middle, and half of the ring finger. Symptoms often worsen at night or when holding a phone. According to guidance from the [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/carpal-tunnel-syndrome/symptoms-causes/syc-20355603), many cases are made worse by repetitive motion and poor upper-body posture, which is why we evaluate the entire neck and shoulder chain rather than just the wrist. Learn more on our [carpal tunnel care page](/services/chiropractic/extremities/carpal-tunnel/).

## Sciatica

Sciatica is irritation of the sciatic nerve, the longest nerve in the body, which starts in the lower back and travels down the leg. Pain, numbness, or tingling typically runs from the buttock down the back of the thigh, and may extend all the way to the foot. Sciatica is usually one-sided and often worsens with sitting, bending, or coughing.

## Peripheral Neuropathy

True peripheral neuropathy is nerve damage stemming from systemic causes, most commonly diabetes. Symptoms tend to appear symmetrically in both feet or both hands and progress slowly over time. The sensation is often described as a stocking-and-glove pattern of numbness or burning. While the underlying nerve damage typically requires medical management, chiropractic care can address the secondary spinal issues that often accompany neuropathy and add to the discomfort.

Sorting out which of these you are actually dealing with requires a thorough evaluation, which is exactly what your first visit covers. Our complete [chiropractic services](/services/chiropractic/) are designed to evaluate the full picture before any care plan begins.

## When to Seek Immediate Care vs. Scheduled Chiropractic Treatment

Most numbness and tingling cases are not emergencies, but a few warning signs do require immediate medical attention rather than a chiropractic appointment. For more on knowing when fast care is appropriate, see our guide to [emergency chiropractic care in Lenexa](/patients/blog/emergency-chiropractic-care-lenexa-same-day-relief-acute-back-pain/).

Seek emergency care immediately if you experience:

- Sudden numbness or weakness on one side of the body (possible stroke)

- Loss of bowel or bladder control along with leg numbness (possible cauda equina syndrome)

- Numbness following a head, neck, or back injury

- Severe, unrelenting pain with progressive weakness

- Numbness accompanied by slurred speech, vision changes, or severe headache

For everything else, scheduled chiropractic care is usually the right starting point. Symptoms that have developed gradually, come and go with activity or posture, follow a clear nerve path, or stem from a known previous injury are exactly what conservative chiropractic care is built to address. If your nerve symptoms began after a car accident, our [auto injury relief](/services/auto-injury-relief/) care includes specific protocols for whiplash and related nerve irritation.

## What Chiropractic Treatment Looks Like at Our Lenexa Office

Your first visit starts with a thorough conversation about your symptoms: when they began, what makes them better or worse, where exactly the numbness or tingling shows up, and any past injuries or health conditions that might be involved. From there, Dr. Meylor performs a complete physical and neurological evaluation, including orthopedic testing, nerve reflex checks, and posture analysis.

If imaging is needed to confirm a diagnosis or rule out other issues, digital X-rays can be performed in our office. Once we have a clear picture, your care plan may include any combination of:

- Targeted spinal adjustments to restore proper motion and relieve nerve compression

- Soft tissue therapy to release the muscles surrounding the affected area

- Flexion-distraction techniques for disc-related nerve compression

- Acupuncture to calm chronic nerve irritation and reduce inflammation

- Corrective exercises to address the postural patterns driving the problem

- Ergonomic and lifestyle guidance to prevent symptoms from returning

For patients whose nerve symptoms are tied to lingering inflammation, our [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/) often pair well with chiropractic adjustments and accelerate relief.

## Get Answers About Your Numbness and Tingling Today

Nerve symptoms rarely improve on their own, and the longer they continue, the harder they can be to reverse. We offer [free consultations](/free-consultation/) and same-day appointments, so you can get a real answer about what is causing your symptoms and a clear plan to resolve them.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Nerve Pain Treatment in Lenexa

**Can chiropractic really help with numbness and tingling?**

Yes, when the symptoms stem from spinal misalignment, disc issues, or nerve compression. These are some of the most common causes of paresthesia, and they respond directly to chiropractic care. If your symptoms have another root cause like uncontrolled diabetes, we will identify that during your evaluation and refer you appropriately.

**How long until I notice improvement?**

It varies based on how long the symptoms have been present and how severe the underlying compression is. Many patients notice meaningful change within the first few visits, while more advanced cases may take several weeks of consistent care before significant relief shows up.

**Do I need imaging before my first visit?**

Not always. Many cases can be evaluated thoroughly without imaging, and if X-rays or other imaging become necessary, we can coordinate that for you. We do not order imaging unnecessarily.

**Is chiropractic safe if I already have a pinched nerve?**

Yes, when performed by a trained chiropractor using techniques appropriate for your condition. Dr. Meylor selects gentle, low-force methods specifically for patients with active nerve compression to avoid aggravating the issue while restoring proper alignment.

**Will my insurance cover care for nerve symptoms?**

Many insurance plans cover chiropractic care for nerve-related conditions including sciatica, radiculopathy, and related diagnoses. Call us at (913) 227-0909 to confirm your specific coverage before your first appointment.

**Can numbness and tingling become permanent if left untreated?**

In some cases, yes. Prolonged nerve compression can lead to lasting nerve damage and muscle weakness. This is why early evaluation matters. Addressing the cause while the nerve is still healthy gives you the best chance of full recovery.

## Visit Our Lenexa Chiropractic Office

Our office is conveniently located at 12980 W 87th St Pkwy in Lenexa, easy to reach from Overland Park, Shawnee, Olathe, and surrounding Johnson County communities. Same-day appointments are often available when nerve symptoms need a fast answer.

content:
Look around any coffee shop, home office, or commuter train in Lenexa and you will see the same posture repeated everywhere: head dropped forward, shoulders rounded, eyes locked on a screen. We spend hours each day in this position, and our bodies are paying the price. The result is a condition so common it has earned its own nickname, tech neck, and for the growing number of remote and hybrid workers in Lenexa, it is becoming one of the most frequent reasons people seek [chiropractic care](/services/chiropractic/).

The good news is that tech neck is highly correctable, especially when caught early. At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, we help office workers, students, and screen-heavy professionals reverse forward head posture, ease the pain it creates, and build habits that keep it from coming back. This guide explains how poor posture develops, why it matters more than most people realize, and what you can do about it both in our office and at home.

## What Is Tech Neck and Why Is It So Common?

Tech neck, sometimes called text neck, is the strain placed on your cervical spine when you tilt your head forward and down to look at phones, laptops, and tablets. The human head weighs roughly 10 to 12 pounds in a neutral position. But here is what most people do not realize: for every inch your head moves forward, the effective load on your neck muscles roughly doubles. At a 45-degree forward tilt, your neck is supporting the equivalent of nearly 50 pounds.

Now multiply that by the hours we spend looking down each day. According to the [Occupational Safety and Health Administration](https://www.osha.gov/etools/computer-workstations), sustained awkward postures are a leading contributor to musculoskeletal strain among computer workers. For the many professionals in Lenexa who shifted to remote or hybrid work, often using makeshift desks at kitchen tables or couches, the problem has accelerated dramatically.

## Common Symptoms of Tech Neck

Forward head posture rarely stays confined to the neck. Watch for these warning signs:

- Aching or stiffness at the base of the neck and upper shoulders

- Tension headaches that start at the back of the skull

- Reduced range of motion when turning your head

- A visible hump developing at the base of the neck

- Tingling or numbness radiating into the arms or hands

- Jaw tension and clenching

- Fatigue and difficulty concentrating late in the workday

Many of these symptoms overlap with conditions we treat regularly, including chronic [neck pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/neck-pain/) and [headaches and migraines](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/headaches-migraines/). Poor sleep often compounds the problem, as detailed in our guide on the [connection between stress, sleep, and spinal health](/patients/blog/stress-sleep-spinal-health-interconnection/), and many patients also benefit from our deeper look at [finding lasting headache and migraine relief at Meylor](/patients/blog/finding-headache-migraine-relief-meylor/). Addressing the underlying posture is what separates lasting relief from temporary fixes.

## How Forward Head Posture Creates Cascading Pain Patterns

The most important thing to understand about posture is that the body works as a connected chain. A problem in one area never stays put. When your head drifts forward and your shoulders round, a predictable cascade of compensation begins, and it spreads far beyond the neck.

### The Cervical Spine Loses Its Natural Curve

A healthy neck has a gentle backward curve that distributes load efficiently. Forward head posture flattens and eventually reverses this curve, forcing the small muscles and ligaments of the cervical spine to work overtime. Research indexed by the [National Center for Biotechnology Information](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5889545/) links sustained forward head posture to increased neck pain and reduced respiratory function. Over months and years, this accelerates wear on the discs and joints, which is how a posture habit becomes a chronic structural problem.

### The Upper Back Rounds and Stiffens

As the head moves forward, the upper back rounds to compensate. The muscles between the shoulder blades become overstretched and weak, while the chest muscles tighten and shorten. This rounded upper back posture, called thoracic kyphosis, then limits how well you can breathe and reduces shoulder mobility.

### The Lower Back and Hips Compensate

To keep you upright and your eyes level, your lower back and pelvis shift to counterbalance the forward weight of your head. This is why so many patients who come in for neck pain are surprised to learn their nagging [lower back pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/back-pain/) is part of the same chain. Treating only the neck while ignoring this cascade is why so many people never get lasting relief.

## Chiropractic Posture Correction for Lenexa's Remote and Hybrid Workers

Reversing tech neck requires more than a single adjustment. It takes a structured approach that restores normal motion, retrains the supporting muscles, and rebuilds the habits driving the problem. At our [Lenexa office](/lenexa/), Dr. Meylor builds posture correction plans around several components working together.

A typical posture correction approach includes:

- **Spinal adjustments.** Gentle, targeted adjustments restore proper motion to the restricted joints of the cervical and thoracic spine, relieving pressure and helping the spine return toward its natural alignment.

- **Soft tissue therapy.** Targeted muscle work releases the tight chest and neck muscles while reactivating the weakened muscles between the shoulder blades.

- **Corrective exercises.** Specific strengthening and stretching routines retrain your body to hold a healthier posture without conscious effort.

- **Ergonomic guidance.** Practical adjustments to your workstation that remove the daily strain at its source.

- **Acupuncture.** For patients with stubborn muscle tension and headaches, our [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/) can complement adjustments and speed relief.

This combined approach is part of our broader chiropractic care services, which treat the whole person rather than just the symptom. The goal is not just to feel better today but to change the structural pattern so the pain does not keep returning.

## At-Home Stretches to Counter Tech Neck

In-office care creates the foundation, but what you do during your workday matters just as much. These simple movements can be done at your desk or anywhere you work, and they directly counter the forward head pattern.

### Chin Tucks

Sit or stand tall. Gently draw your chin straight back, as if making a double chin, without tilting your head up or down. Hold for five seconds, then release. Repeat 10 times. This is the single most effective movement for retraining forward head posture.

### Doorway Chest Stretch

Stand in a doorway with your forearms resting on the frame, elbows at shoulder height. Step gently forward until you feel a stretch across your chest. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. This opens the tight chest muscles that pull the shoulders forward.

### Upper Trapezius Stretch

Sitting tall, gently tilt your head toward one shoulder until you feel a stretch along the opposite side of your neck. Hold for 20 seconds per side. This relieves the muscle tension that builds up from holding your head forward all day.

### Shoulder Blade Squeezes

Pull your shoulder blades down and back, as if tucking them into your back pockets. Hold for five seconds and repeat 10 times. This reactivates the weakened muscles that posture has switched off.

Aim to take a movement break every 30 to 45 minutes. Even standing and rolling your shoulders for 30 seconds interrupts the static loading that drives tech neck. For a fuller routine, see our [post-Thanksgiving reset guide on moving better to feel better](/patients/blog/post-thanksgiving-reset-move-better-feel-better/).

## Workplace Setup Tips for Lenexa Home Offices

Many of the posture problems we see start with a poorly arranged workspace. A few simple ergonomic changes, supported by guidance from the [Mayo Clinic on office ergonomics](https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/adult-health/in-depth/office-ergonomics/art-20046169), remove the constant downward pull on your neck:

- **Raise your monitor.** The top of your screen should sit at or just below eye level so you look straight ahead, not down.

- **Use an external keyboard with laptops.** Laptops force a choice between a good screen height and a good keyboard height. An external keyboard lets you have both.

- **Support your lower back.** A chair with proper lumbar support keeps your whole spine stacked correctly.

- **Keep feet flat on the floor.** Knees should be roughly level with your hips.

- **Bring your phone up to eye level.** Instead of dropping your head to your phone, raise the phone to you.

- **Position frequently used items within easy reach.** Constant twisting and reaching builds asymmetrical strain.

If you travel for work or the holidays, our tips for [prepping your body for holiday travel stress](/patients/blog/prepping-body-holiday-travel-stress/) help you avoid the posture setbacks that long flights and car rides create. Looking for practical posture-friendly upgrades? Our roundup of [holiday gift ideas that support spinal health](/patients/blog/holiday-gift-ideas-support-spinal-health/) covers ergonomic tools we recommend to patients year-round.

If your posture issues trace back to a previous injury rather than just work habits, our [auto injury relief](/services/auto-injury-relief/) care addresses the alignment problems that car accidents commonly leave behind.

## Start Standing Taller, Living Pain-Free

Tech neck only gets harder to reverse the longer you wait. Our Lenexa office offers [free consultations](/free-consultation/) and same-day appointments, so you can get a clear answer about your posture and a real plan to fix it. If your pain has already become severe, our [emergency chiropractic care for same-day acute back pain relief](/patients/blog/emergency-chiropractic-care-lenexa-same-day-relief-acute-back-pain/) is available, and if you want to make posture a long-term priority, learn [why now is the right time to begin a 2026 spinal wellness plan](/patients/blog/why-begin-2026-spinal-wellness-plan/). Take the first step today.

Schedule Free Consultation Call (913) 227-0909

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can tech neck really be reversed, or just managed?

In most cases, especially when addressed early, forward head posture can be meaningfully corrected. The combination of chiropractic adjustments, corrective exercises, and ergonomic changes can restore much of the cervical curve and relieve the associated pain. Long-standing, severe cases may not fully reverse but almost always improve significantly.

### How long does posture correction take?

It depends on how long the posture pattern has been developing and how consistent you are with care and home exercises. Many patients feel noticeably better within a few weeks, while true structural change typically unfolds over two to four months of consistent care.

### Is chiropractic adjustment safe for neck and posture issues?

Yes. Dr. Meylor uses techniques appropriate for each patient, including gentle and low-force options when needed. A thorough evaluation always comes first to identify the safest, most effective approach for your specific situation.

### I work from home. Do you offer ergonomic advice for my setup?

Absolutely. Ergonomic guidance is a core part of posture correction. We help you arrange your home workspace so it stops feeding the problem, which is essential for lasting results.

### Will my insurance cover posture-related chiropractic care?

Many insurance plans cover chiropractic care for neck pain and related posture conditions. We accept a wide range of plans and recommend calling us at (913) 227-0909 to confirm your coverage before your first visit.

### Do I need a referral to come in?

No referral is needed to see a chiropractor in Kansas. You can call us directly to schedule a free consultation and get started right away.

## Visit Our Lenexa Chiropractic Office

Our office is conveniently located at 12980 W 87th St Pkwy in Lenexa, easy to reach from Overland Park, Shawnee, Olathe, and surrounding Johnson County communities. Whether you work from home or commute to an office, we make it simple to fit posture care into a busy schedule.

excerpt: If you've ever woken up with a sore jaw, heard clicking or popping when you chew, or dealt with persistent headaches, you may be living with TMJ disorder. Learn how chiropractic care at Meylor Chiropractic in Lenexa can offer real, lasting relief.
content:
If you've ever woken up with a sore jaw, heard a clicking or popping sound when you chew, or dealt with persistent headaches that seem to have no clear cause, you may be living with TMJ disorder — and you're not alone. Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) dysfunction is one of the most overlooked sources of chronic pain, and many Lenexa residents don't realize that [chiropractic care](/services/chiropractic/) can offer real, lasting relief.

At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture in Lenexa, Dr. Meylor has helped patients throughout the Lenexa and Johnson County area find relief from jaw pain using a whole-body approach that addresses the root cause of TMJ symptoms — not just the discomfort itself.

## What Is TMJ Disorder?

The temporomandibular joint is the hinge that connects your jaw to the temporal bones of your skull, just in front of each ear. It's one of the most complex joints in your body — it allows your jaw to move up and down, side to side, and forward and back. When this joint becomes inflamed, misaligned, or strained, the result is TMJ disorder (also called TMD).

TMJ disorder affects an estimated [10 to 35 million Americans](https://www.nidcr.nih.gov/health-info/tmj), and it's more common in adults between the ages of 20 and 40. For many Lenexa residents, the symptoms appear gradually and are often mistaken for dental problems, tension headaches, or even ear infections.

TMJ is not just a dental issue. The jaw, neck, and spine are deeply interconnected — which is exactly why a chiropractic approach can be so effective.

## Recognizing the Symptoms of TMJ Dysfunction

Because TMJ affects a joint that's in constant motion — every time you eat, talk, or yawn — symptoms can be wide-ranging and easy to misattribute. Common signs of TMJ disorder include:

- A clicking, popping, or grinding sound when you open or close your mouth

- Pain or tenderness in the jaw, especially near the ear or temple

- Difficulty or discomfort while chewing or biting

- Jaw locking — the feeling that your jaw has "gotten stuck" open or closed

- Facial pain or soreness that worsens throughout the day

- Frequent headaches, particularly around the temples or base of the skull

- Earaches, ringing in the ears (tinnitus), or a sense of fullness in the ears

- [Neck stiffness](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/neck-pain/) or shoulder tension

If you're experiencing several of these symptoms and you live in the Lenexa area, it's worth speaking with a provider who understands the connection between jaw function and spinal alignment. That connection is central to how Dr. Meylor approaches TMJ care.

## The Connection Between Neck Alignment and TMJ

One of the most important — and most underappreciated — aspects of TMJ dysfunction is how closely the jaw is connected to the neck and upper spine. The muscles, nerves, and joints of the jaw don't operate in isolation. They are biomechanically linked to the cervical spine (your neck), and tension or misalignment in one area often creates problems in the other.

When the vertebrae in your upper neck are out of alignment, the surrounding muscles and nerves are affected. The muscles that control jaw movement — including the masseter, temporalis, and pterygoid muscles — are innervated by the [trigeminal nerve](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/trigeminal-neuralgia), which also has connections through the brainstem and upper cervical region. A misaligned cervical spine can create tension and irritation that radiates into the jaw, contributing to or worsening TMJ symptoms.

Conversely, a chronically tense or misaligned jaw can place strain on the muscles of the neck and upper back, creating a cycle of pain that's difficult to break without addressing the structural causes.

For many Lenexa patients, treating the neck and upper spine is the missing piece in their TMJ care — and it's where chiropractic care makes a meaningful difference.

## Common Postural Factors

Poor posture — particularly "forward head posture," which is increasingly common with extended screen and phone use — is a significant contributing factor in many TMJ cases. When your head shifts forward, the muscles at the base of your skull and upper neck become chronically overloaded. This tension can travel into the jaw and contribute to grinding, clenching, and joint dysfunction.

For Lenexa residents who spend long hours at a desk or commuting, postural imbalances are something Dr. Meylor evaluates as part of every TMJ assessment.

## How Chiropractic Care Addresses TMJ in Lenexa

When you come to Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture for a TMJ evaluation, Dr. Meylor begins with a thorough assessment — not just of the jaw, but of the entire spine and posture. He looks at how the head sits on the neck, whether there are restrictions or misalignments in the cervical vertebrae, and how the muscles and soft tissues of the jaw and neck are functioning.

Treatment is tailored to what's actually driving your symptoms. Depending on your presentation, a care plan for TMJ in Lenexa may include:

**Cervical Chiropractic Adjustments**

Precise, gentle adjustments to the upper cervical spine help restore proper alignment and reduce the muscular tension that contributes to jaw dysfunction. Many patients notice a reduction in jaw pain and headache frequency after addressing restrictions in the neck — even before any direct jaw work is performed.

**Soft Tissue Therapy**

The muscles around the jaw are often chronically tight in people with TMJ. Releasing trigger points and tension in the masseter and temporalis muscles — combined with neck and shoulder work — can bring significant relief and restore more natural jaw movement.

**TMJ-Specific Joint Mobilization**

Dr. Meylor is trained in gentle mobilization techniques for the temporomandibular joint itself. These techniques help restore range of motion, reduce inflammation within the joint, and improve the coordination of jaw movement.

**Postural Correction and Ergonomic Guidance**

Addressing the root causes means helping Lenexa patients understand how their daily habits contribute to jaw and neck tension. Dr. Meylor provides guidance on workspace setup, sleep positions, and exercises that support lasting improvement.

**Acupuncture for TMJ Relief**

For patients dealing with significant muscle tension, inflammation, or stress-related jaw clenching, acupuncture is an excellent complementary treatment. Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture offers [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/) as part of integrative TMJ care, targeting the muscles and meridians associated with jaw and facial pain. Many Lenexa patients find acupuncture helps them break the stress-clenching cycle more quickly.

## TMJ and Headaches: Understanding the Link

Headaches are one of the most frequently reported symptoms by patients with TMJ disorder — and one of the most frustrating, because they're often treated in isolation without addressing the jaw. Tension-type headaches that originate from the temporomandibular joint or the muscles around it are sometimes called [cervicogenic headaches](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/headaches-migraines/), meaning they stem from the cervical spine and surrounding structures.

For Lenexa residents who deal with recurring headaches and haven't found relief through standard treatments, TMJ dysfunction is worth evaluating as a contributing cause. Chiropractic care that addresses both the jaw and the neck can reduce headache frequency significantly for many patients.

## What to Expect as a New Patient in Lenexa

If you're new to Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, your first visit begins with a conversation. Dr. Meylor takes time to understand your symptoms, your history, and what you've already tried. He performs a physical examination that looks at your jaw function, cervical range of motion, posture, and relevant neurological indicators.

You won't be rushed. Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture is a patient-first practice that has served the Lenexa community since 2005, and the approach reflects that commitment. Most new patients leave their first appointment with a clear understanding of what's contributing to their TMJ symptoms and a personalized plan for addressing it.

Same-day appointments are often available, and the office accepts most major insurance plans — call to confirm your coverage.

## Ready to Find Relief from Jaw Pain in Lenexa?

You don't have to keep living with clicking, aching, or restricted jaw movement. If you're in [Lenexa](/lenexa/) or the surrounding Johnson County area and you're ready to get to the root of your TMJ symptoms, Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture is here to help.

Call Dr. Meylor today: (913) 227-0909 Or visit www.meylorchiro.com/free-consultation to request your free consultation.

content:
A herniated disc can turn everyday life into a struggle. Simple movements like getting out of bed, bending over, sitting at a desk, or driving across town can suddenly become painful. For many people, the discomfort is not limited to the back. A herniated disc may also cause shooting pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness that travels into the hips, legs, or feet.

At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, we help patients in Lenexa find conservative, non-surgical options for disc-related pain whenever appropriate. If you are searching for a herniated disc chiropractor Lenexa residents trust or looking for bulging disc treatment, our goal is to help you understand what is happening, relieve pressure where possible, and support healing through personalized [chiropractic care](/services/chiropractic/).

Located in Lenexa, our office works with patients who want real solutions for serious back conditions without automatically jumping to invasive procedures. For many people, conservative care can play an important role in reducing pain, improving mobility, and helping them return to daily activities with greater comfort.

## What Is a Herniated Disc?

Your spine is made up of bones called vertebrae, and between those bones are discs that act like cushions. These discs help absorb shock, support movement, and keep the spine flexible. Each disc has a softer inner center and a tougher outer layer.

A herniated disc happens when the inner material pushes outward through a weakened or damaged part of the outer layer. Some people may also hear the terms bulging disc, slipped disc, or ruptured disc. While these terms are often used interchangeably in casual conversation, they are not always exactly the same. In general, they all describe some level of disc dysfunction that may put pressure on nearby nerves or spinal structures.

When that pressure occurs, symptoms can range from mild discomfort to severe, radiating pain. In many cases, a herniated disc in the lower back is what causes pain to travel down the leg, sometimes referred to as [sciatica](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/sciatica/). According to the [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/herniated-disk/symptoms-causes/syc-20354095), most herniated discs occur in the lumbar spine.

For patients in Lenexa, understanding the source of pain is the first step toward finding the right treatment path.

## Common Symptoms of a Herniated Disc

A herniated disc does not always feel the same for every person. Some people experience localized back pain, while others feel more nerve-related symptoms because the disc is irritating a nearby nerve root.

Common symptoms may include:

- Sharp or shooting pain in the back
- Pain that radiates into the buttock, hip, or leg
- Numbness or tingling
- Burning sensations
- Muscle weakness
- Pain that worsens with sitting, bending, or lifting
- Difficulty standing fully upright
- Discomfort when coughing or sneezing

For some people in Lenexa, persistent [lower back pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/back-pain/) often starts suddenly after lifting something heavy or twisting awkwardly. For others, the problem develops gradually over time because of repeated stress, poor movement mechanics, or wear and tear.

If you are noticing ongoing radiating pain or numbness, it is important not to ignore it. Disc-related symptoms often require more than rest alone.

## What Causes a Herniated or Bulging Disc?

Disc problems can happen for several reasons. Sometimes they are related to a specific event, but often they result from a combination of factors that build up over time.

Common causes and contributing factors include:

- Repetitive bending or lifting
- Sudden twisting movements
- Poor posture
- Prolonged sitting
- Physically demanding work
- Sports injuries
- Age-related disc degeneration
- Weak supporting muscles
- Previous back injuries

Patients in [Lenexa](/lenexa/) often come in after the pain begins interfering with work, sleep, exercise, or family life. Whether the issue came on quickly or developed slowly, the key is determining how severe it is and whether conservative care is appropriate.

## How a Herniated Disc Affects Daily Life

A herniated disc can affect far more than your back. It can change the way you move, how long you can sit, and whether you can comfortably do your job or enjoy normal routines.

People with disc-related pain often struggle with:

- Sitting through a workday
- Driving for long periods
- Sleeping comfortably
- Picking up children
- Getting dressed
- Exercising or walking
- Household chores
- Standing for long periods

For many patients in Lenexa, the frustration comes not only from the pain but also from how unpredictable it feels. Some days are manageable, while others are much worse. That uncertainty is one reason many people begin looking for a herniated disc chiropractor Lenexa patients trust for a more targeted solution.

## Non-Surgical Chiropractic Relief for Herniated Discs

The good news is that surgery is not always the first or only answer. Many patients with disc-related pain improve with [conservative care](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3915599/), especially when the condition is identified early and managed appropriately.

At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, non-surgical chiropractic care focuses on helping reduce irritation, improve spinal function, and support the body's natural healing processes. The goal is not to force the disc back into place with a quick fix. Instead, treatment is designed to address spinal mechanics, reduce stress on affected areas, and help patients move more comfortably.

Conservative chiropractic care may help support:

- Improved spinal motion
- Reduced joint restriction
- Less pressure on irritated structures
- Better mobility and posture
- Reduced muscle guarding and tension
- Improved function during daily activities

For patients searching for bulging disc treatment in Lenexa, chiropractic care can be an important option when symptoms are appropriate for conservative management.

## How Chiropractic Care May Help Disc-Related Pain

When a disc is irritated, the body often compensates in multiple ways. Muscles tighten, posture changes, movement becomes guarded, and nearby joints may stop moving properly. This creates a cycle where pain leads to compensation, and compensation leads to more irritation.

Chiropractic care aims to improve how the spine and surrounding joints function so the body can move more normally again. By addressing restricted motion and mechanical stress, patients may experience improvements in both pain and mobility.

At our Lenexa office, care is personalized based on the patient's symptoms, history, and overall presentation. No two disc cases are exactly alike, which is why a one-size-fits-all approach is not appropriate for this kind of condition.

## Conservative Care vs. Immediate Surgery

Many people worry that a herniated disc automatically means surgery. In reality, many disc injuries are first managed with conservative treatment unless there are serious neurological concerns or emergency symptoms.

Conservative care may be appropriate when:

- Pain is present but manageable
- Symptoms are irritating daily life but not rapidly worsening
- There is numbness or tingling without major loss of function
- The patient is still able to move and perform basic tasks
- No emergency red flags are present

For many patients in Lenexa, starting with conservative care makes sense because it allows the body a chance to heal and respond without the risks or recovery time associated with surgery.

This is why people often seek a herniated disc chiropractor Lenexa patients can see quickly when they want to explore non-surgical relief first.

## When Surgery Might Be Necessary

While conservative care is often a good first step, surgery may be necessary in certain situations. This is especially true when there are signs of severe nerve compromise or emergency symptoms that require immediate medical attention.

Surgery may be more strongly considered when a patient has:

- Severe or progressive muscle weakness
- Loss of bowel or bladder control
- Numbness in the saddle area
- Severe neurological deficits
- Pain that does not respond to appropriate conservative care
- Disc damage confirmed to require surgical evaluation

These situations should not be ignored. If symptoms suggest significant nerve involvement or a medical emergency, prompt medical evaluation is essential.

At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, patient safety comes first. Conservative care has an important role, but it is also important to recognize when a patient needs imaging, referral, or a higher level of medical intervention.

## Why Personalized Care Matters

A disc problem is not just about one painful structure. It affects the way the entire body moves. One person may have intense leg pain with very little back pain. Another may have mostly stiffness and numbness. Someone else may have a bulging disc with recurring flare-ups tied to work or sitting posture. Complementary therapies such as [acupuncture](/services/acupuncture/) may also support recovery.

That is why personalized care matters.

At our Lenexa office, treatment is based on:

- The location of the disc issue
- The severity of symptoms
- Whether pain is local or radiating
- Movement limitations
- Daily activity demands
- Overall health history
- Response to previous treatment

Patients looking for bulging disc treatment often need more than generic advice. They need a plan that fits their condition, their schedule, and their goals.

## Supporting Recovery and Preventing Flare-Ups

Relief is important, but long-term improvement also involves preventing the same problem from coming back. Once a disc has been irritated, the body may remain vulnerable if the same stress patterns continue.

Recovery support often includes attention to:

- Posture
- Body mechanics
- Lifting habits
- Sitting tolerance
- Flexibility
- Core support
- Movement patterns during work and home activities

For patients in Lenexa, this practical side of care can be just as important as in-office treatment. A long-term plan should help reduce recurrence, not just get through the current flare-up.

## Choosing Conservative Disc Care in Lenexa

When back pain becomes severe or starts traveling into the leg, many people begin searching for help immediately. They want answers, relief, and a clear plan. They also want to know whether surgery can be avoided.

At Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture, we provide conservative, non-surgical support for patients in Lenexa dealing with herniated discs, bulging discs, and serious back pain conditions. Our focus is on helping patients understand their options and pursue appropriate chiropractic care when conservative treatment is a good fit.

If you have been searching for a herniated disc chiropractor Lenexa residents can trust, we are here to help you take the next step toward relief.

## Visit Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture

If you are dealing with shooting pain, numbness, tingling, or back pain that may be connected to a disc issue, do not wait for it to take over your routine. Conservative chiropractic care may help support recovery and improve your quality of life.
