content:
Most people who are curious about acupuncture never book the first appointment. It is rarely because they doubt it could help. It is because they do not know what will happen once they walk through the door. Will it hurt? How long does it take? What should I wear? Will I be pressured into a long treatment plan? That uncertainty is enough to keep a lot of people from ever trying it.

This guide removes the guesswork. It walks through a first visit at Meylor Chiropractic and Acupuncture from the moment you call to the moment you leave, so you know exactly what to expect before you arrive. No surprises, no pressure, and no mystery.

## Before Your Visit: Booking and Preparation

Your first step is a phone call or an online request for a free consultation. When you reach our Lenexa office, our team will ask a few quick questions about what brings you in, check whether your insurance may apply, and find a time that works for your schedule. If you want to understand the basics of the practice before you call, our guide on [what acupuncture is and how it works](/patients/blog/acupuncture-explained-how-does-it-work-lenexa/) is a good place to start.

### How to Prepare

- Eat a light meal beforehand. Arriving on an empty stomach can leave some people feeling lightheaded.
- Wear loose, comfortable clothing. Many common points are on the arms and lower legs, so clothing you can easily roll up works best.
- Bring a list of medications. This matters especially if you take blood thinners.
- Note your symptoms. When they started, what makes them better or worse, and what you have already tried.
- Arrive a few minutes early. This gives you time to complete intake paperwork without feeling rushed.

## Step 1: Arrival and Intake

When you arrive at our Lenexa office, our front desk team will greet you and help you complete a short health history form. This covers your current symptoms, medical history, medications, sleep, stress levels, and goals. It is not busywork. Everything on that form helps shape a treatment plan built for you rather than a generic routine.

If you are also dealing with musculoskeletal issues, this is the time to mention it. Because we offer both acupuncture and [chiropractic care](/services/chiropractic/), we can look at the full picture and coordinate the two when that serves you better.

## Step 2: The Consultation

Before any needles are involved, you sit down with Dr. Meylor for a conversation. This is the most important part of your first visit. Expect questions about the problem that brought you in, how it affects your daily life, and what you hope to change.

This is also your time to ask questions. Ask how acupuncture might help your specific concern, how many sessions are typical, and what realistic results look like. You will get straight answers. If acupuncture is not the right fit for your situation, you will hear that too, along with a recommendation for what might serve you better.

### Safety Screening

Part of the consultation is making sure acupuncture is safe for you. According to the [National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/acupuncture-what-you-need-to-know), acupuncture has a good safety record when performed by a trained practitioner using sterile needles, though certain conditions such as bleeding disorders call for extra care. We screen for these before treatment begins.

## Step 3: Your First Treatment

Once your plan is set, you move to a private, quiet treatment room. You lie comfortably on a padded table, face up or face down depending on the points being used, with blankets and pillows for support.

### Needle Placement

Dr. Meylor places very thin, single-use sterile needles at specific points. These needles are about the width of a human hair and nothing like the needles used for shots or blood draws. Most people feel a brief tap at insertion, followed by a mild sensation of pressure, warmth, or heaviness. Many are surprised that some points are far from where their symptoms are located, which is normal and intentional.

### The Resting Period

The needles typically stay in place for 15 to 30 minutes while you rest. The room is kept calm and quiet. This is the part most patients love. Many describe a deep sense of relaxation, and it is common to drift off to sleep. If you feel uncomfortable at any point, you simply say so and adjustments are made right away.

### Needle Removal

Removal is quick and usually painless. The needles are disposed of immediately in a medical sharps container. They are never reused.

## Step 4: After Your Session

After treatment, we check in about how you feel and go over any recommendations to support your progress at home, such as hydration, gentle movement, or stretching. Most people leave feeling calm and relaxed. Some notice immediate relief, while others notice gradual changes over the following days.

Mild effects such as slight tiredness or minor tenderness at a needle site can happen and usually fade within a day. The [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/acupuncture/about/pac-20392763) notes that side effects from acupuncture performed by a competent practitioner are generally mild. You can typically return to normal activities right away.

If a follow-up plan makes sense, we will explain the recommended frequency and why. You are never obligated to commit to a package on your first visit.

## What a First Visit Costs and What Is Included

Cost is one of the most common questions new patients in Lenexa ask, and the answer is simpler than most expect. Your session fee covers everything: the consultation, the treatment itself, and all needles and supplies. There is no separate charge for acupuncture needles, and every needle is single-use and sterile.

**Cost tip:** Many insurance plans now include some acupuncture coverage, especially for pain-related conditions, and HSA and FSA funds typically apply. Our team can help you check your benefits before you book, so you know what to expect financially.

For a full breakdown of coverage and pricing, read our guide on [whether insurance covers acupuncture](/patients/blog/does-insurance-cover-acupuncture-lenexa/). You can also learn more about our [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/) and the conditions we most often help with, including [chronic back pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/back-pain/) and [headaches and migraines](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/headaches-migraines/).

## Why Our Lenexa Wellness Center Feels Different

A good first visit is about more than technique. It is about feeling comfortable, informed, and respected. That is what we aim for with every new patient in Lenexa. You get time to ask questions, a clear explanation of what is happening and why, honest guidance about whether acupuncture fits your needs, and a calm space designed for rest. And because acupuncture and chiropractic care are offered under one roof, your care can be coordinated rather than split across different offices.

## Ready for Your First Acupuncture Visit?

Now that you know exactly what to expect, the only step left is booking. Schedule a free consultation at our Lenexa wellness center, ask every question you have, and decide with confidence. No pressure and no obligation.

[Schedule Free Consultation](/free-consultation/) Call (913) 227-0909

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does a first acupuncture visit take?**

Plan on about 60 minutes for your first visit, which includes intake, consultation, and treatment. Follow-up sessions usually run 30 to 45 minutes.

**Does the first acupuncture session hurt?**

Most patients feel very little. The needles are hair-thin, and the most common sensation is a brief tap followed by mild pressure or warmth. Many people find the session deeply relaxing.

**Do I pay extra for the acupuncture needles?**

No. Needles are single-use, sterile, and always included in your session fee. You never pay separately for them.

**Do I need to undress for acupuncture?**

Usually not. Many points can be reached by rolling up sleeves or pant legs, which is why loose clothing is recommended. If other areas need access, you will be draped appropriately and your comfort always comes first.

**Will I be pressured to buy a treatment package?**

No. We will explain what we recommend and why, but you are never required to commit to a package on your first visit.

**Can I drive home after my session?**

Yes, most people can return to normal activities right away, including driving. If you ever feel lightheaded, you are welcome to rest in the office until you feel ready.

## Visit Our Lenexa Acupuncture Wellness Center

Our office is conveniently located at 12980 W 87th St Pkwy in Lenexa, easy to reach from Overland Park, Shawnee, Olathe, and surrounding Johnson County communities. We look forward to welcoming you for your first visit.

title: What Does a Chiropractor Do?
excerpt: What does a chiropractor do? A plain-English guide to adjustments, conditions treated, and what to expect at a Lenexa visit. Call (913) 227-0909.
content:
Ask ten people what a chiropractor actually does and you will get ten different answers. Some picture dramatic back cracking. Others assume it is only for back pain. A few are not sure whether it counts as real healthcare at all. Those gaps in understanding are the single most common reason people in Lenexa put off care that could have helped them months earlier.

The honest answer is more practical and less mysterious than most expect. This guide explains what chiropractors are trained to do, which conditions we treat most often, what happens during a visit, and just as importantly, when chiropractic is not the right answer for your situation.

## What a Chiropractor Is Trained to Do

A Doctor of Chiropractic is a licensed healthcare provider who diagnoses and treats disorders of the musculoskeletal system, with particular focus on the spine and how it affects the nervous system. Training covers anatomy, physiology, neurology, orthopedics, diagnostic imaging, and hands-on clinical practice.

In day-to-day practice, the work breaks into four parts: evaluating how your body moves and where it does not, identifying the mechanical source of your symptoms, applying hands-on treatment to restore normal function, and giving you the exercises and habits that keep the problem from returning.

The [National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/chiropractic-in-depth) describes chiropractic as a licensed healthcare profession whose practitioners use hands-on spinal manipulation along with other treatments, and notes that spinal manipulation is among the most studied of these approaches. It is a regulated clinical profession, not an alternative fringe practice.

### The Core Idea Behind the Work

Your spine does two jobs at once. It carries load and allows movement, and it houses the nervous system that controls everything else. When a spinal joint stops moving properly, the effects are not limited to that one spot. Surrounding muscles tighten protectively, nearby nerves can become irritated, inflammation builds, and the rest of the body starts compensating in ways that create new problems.

Chiropractic care interrupts that chain. Rather than treating the pain where you feel it, the goal is to find and correct the mechanical dysfunction producing it.

## What Chiropractors Actually Treat

The pattern we see most often in Lenexa is not dramatic injury. It is the accumulation of ordinary strain: desk work, poor sleep positions, weekend yard work, and old injuries that never fully resolved. The conditions that bring people in most frequently include:

- **Lower back pain.** The most common reason patients seek chiropractic care anywhere, and the condition with the strongest research support. See our approach to [chronic back pain](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/back-pain/).
- **Neck pain and stiffness.** Increasingly driven by screen posture. Our [neck pain care](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/neck-pain/) addresses both the joints and the muscles involved.
- **Tension headaches.** Frequently originating from cervical restriction rather than anything in the head itself.
- **Sciatica and radiating pain.** When nerve irritation stems from the lumbar spine, addressed through targeted [sciatica care](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/sciatica/).
- **Joint pain in the shoulders, hips, and knees.** Extremity joints respond to the same principles as the spine.
- **Post-accident injuries.** Including whiplash and the alignment changes collisions leave behind.
- **Reduced mobility and stiffness.** Often the earliest sign of a problem, and the easiest stage to correct.

## What Happens During a Chiropractic Visit

Knowing the sequence removes most of the hesitation people feel before a first appointment.

### Evaluation Before Anything Else

No treatment happens without an assessment. Dr. Meylor reviews your health history, then evaluates posture, range of motion, joint restriction, muscle tone, and neurological signs such as reflexes and sensation. This determines whether chiropractic care is appropriate for you at all, and if so, which technique fits.

### The Adjustment

A chiropractic adjustment is a precise, controlled force applied to one specific joint to restore its normal motion. It takes a fraction of a second. Most patients describe brief pressure followed by a sense of release. The popping sound that sometimes accompanies it is gas releasing from the joint fluid, not bones cracking, and an effective adjustment does not always produce one.

### Technique Is Chosen for the Patient

Chiropractic is not one technique applied identically to everyone. The method is selected based on your age, condition, and comfort level:

- **Diversified technique.** The traditional manual adjustment using a quick, specific thrust.
- **Activator method.** A handheld instrument delivering a gentle low-force impulse with no twisting, well suited to seniors and patients with arthritis.
- **Drop table.** A section of the table drops slightly so very little force is required.
- **Flexion-distraction.** Gentle rhythmic decompression used for [disc-related injuries](/services/chiropractic/injuries/disc-injury/).
- **Soft tissue work.** Muscle release that accompanies adjustments to reduce surrounding tension.

### Beyond the Adjustment

Adjustments alone rarely produce lasting change. What holds the correction is what happens between visits: corrective exercises, ergonomic changes, and movement habits. Our full [chiropractic care services](/services/chiropractic/) include this guidance as standard rather than as an upsell.

## Where Chiropractic Fits in Holistic Health Approaches

Chiropractic works best as one part of a broader picture rather than a standalone fix. Structure, nervous system regulation, movement, sleep, and stress all influence how you feel, and treating one while ignoring the rest limits results.

That is why many patients in Lenexa combine chiropractic with [acupuncture care](/services/acupuncture/), which addresses inflammation and nervous system regulation from a different angle. Adjustments correct the mechanics. Acupuncture calms the pain signaling and stress response layered on top of them. Together they cover ground neither reaches alone.

## When Chiropractic Is Not the Right Answer

Being straight about limitations matters more than being persuasive. Chiropractic care is effective for mechanical musculoskeletal problems. It is not a treatment for infection, cancer, fractures, or systemic disease, and it does not replace necessary medical care.

**Seek emergency medical care instead of booking an adjustment if you have:** sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body, loss of bowel or bladder control alongside back or leg symptoms, severe unrelenting pain following significant trauma, signs of infection such as fever with back pain, or numbness accompanied by vision changes or slurred speech.

Certain conditions also call for modified technique or make manipulation inappropriate, including severe osteoporosis, spinal tumors, some bone abnormalities, and elevated stroke risk. The [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/chiropractic-adjustment/about/pac-20393513) notes that chiropractic adjustment is generally safe when performed by a trained, licensed practitioner, and that evaluation should always precede treatment. This is exactly why the assessment is never skipped, and why we refer patients elsewhere when their situation calls for it.

## Have Questions? Ask Before You Commit

If you are still unsure whether chiropractic care fits your situation, a conversation costs nothing. We offer free consultations at our Lenexa office so you can get a straight assessment before making any decision.

**What does a chiropractor do on the first visit?**

The first visit is mostly evaluation. Dr. Meylor reviews your health history, assesses posture, range of motion, joint function, and neurological signs, then explains what is driving your symptoms. Treatment follows only if chiropractic care is appropriate for your condition.

**Is a chiropractor a real doctor?**

A Doctor of Chiropractic is a licensed healthcare provider who completes doctoral-level training in anatomy, neurology, orthopedics, diagnosis, and imaging. Chiropractors are licensed and regulated in every state, including Kansas.

**Do chiropractors only treat back pain?**

No. Back pain is the most common reason people come in, but chiropractors also treat neck pain, tension headaches, sciatica, extremity joint problems, post-accident injuries, and mobility restriction.

**Does a chiropractic adjustment hurt?**

For most patients, no. The common description is brief pressure followed by relief. Mild soreness for a day afterward is normal, similar to after exercise. Gentle low-force techniques are available if you are concerned about discomfort.

**Do I need a referral to see a chiropractor in Kansas?**

No referral is required. You can call our Lenexa office directly at (913) 227-0909 to schedule a free consultation.

**How do I know if I need a chiropractor or a medical doctor?**

If your pain is mechanical, meaning it changes with movement or position and followed strain, posture, or injury, chiropractic care is a reasonable starting point. If you have fever, unexplained weight loss, progressive weakness, or the emergency signs listed above, see a physician first. We will refer you if your evaluation points that direction.

- **[Back pain care](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/back-pain/).** Acute strain, chronic low back pain, and the recurring flare-ups that follow lifting, sitting, or old injuries.
- **[Neck pain care](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/neck-pain/).** Stiffness, restricted rotation, and the forward head posture that comes with screen work.
- **[Sciatica care](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/sciatica/).** Radiating pain, numbness, or tingling running from the lower back into the leg.
- **[Headache and migraine care](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/headaches-migraines/).** Tension headaches that originate from cervical restriction rather than the head itself.
- **[Disc injury care](/services/chiropractic/injuries/disc-injury/).** Bulges and herniations, typically managed with flexion-distraction rather than forceful technique.

### Acupuncture

Our [acupuncture services](/services/acupuncture/) work through the nervous system rather than the skeleton, which makes them a useful complement to adjustments. Patients most often use acupuncture for chronic pain that has not fully responded to other care, stress and tension, sleep problems, and inflammation. Sessions use single-use sterile needles, and the cost of needles is always included in the visit fee.

### Injury Recovery

Our [auto injury relief care](/services/auto-injury-relief/) addresses whiplash, post-collision neck and back pain, and the delayed symptoms that commonly surface two or three days after an accident. Many auto policies include medical coverage that applies here, and our team can help you check.

### Performance Care

Our [golf performance care](/services/golf/) focuses on the rotational mobility, hip function, and spinal mechanics that golf demands. It suits recreational players dealing with pain as well as those simply trying to protect their swing.

## Which Chiropractic Service Is Right for My Condition?

The honest answer is that an evaluation decides this, not a web page. But a few patterns hold true, and they are a reasonable starting point:

- Pain that changes with movement or position is usually mechanical and responds well to adjustments.
- Pain that radiates into an arm or leg suggests nerve involvement and points toward sciatica or disc-focused care.
- Pain layered with high stress, poor sleep, or inflammation often benefits from acupuncture alongside chiropractic.
- Pain that started after a collision belongs in auto injury care, and early evaluation matters more here than almost anywhere else.
- Stiffness without real pain is the easiest stage to correct and the one most people ignore until it worsens.

The pattern we see most often in Lenexa is a combination rather than a single clean category. Someone with a desk job and a decade-old back injury rarely fits one box, which is why the first visit is an evaluation rather than a treatment.

**Worth knowing:** HSA and FSA funds typically apply to both chiropractic and acupuncture. If your deductible is already met for the year, late-year care often costs noticeably less out of pocket than the same care in January.

Our team verifies benefits regularly and can walk you through what your plan covers before you commit to anything. Consultations are free, so there is no financial risk in simply asking.

Chiropractic care treats mechanical musculoskeletal problems. It does not treat infection, fractures, tumors, or systemic disease, and it is not a substitute for medical care when that is what your situation calls for.

Some conditions also require modified technique or rule manipulation out entirely, including severe osteoporosis, spinal tumors, and elevated stroke risk. If your evaluation points somewhere outside our scope, we will tell you and refer you accordingly.

title: Work Injury Chiropractor in Lenexa: What to Write Down and What the First Visit Covers
excerpt: Need a work injury chiropractor in Lenexa? What to write down after an incident, what Dr. Meylor's first visit covers, and evening appointment options.
content:
Warehouse shifts, desk jobs, delivery routes, and healthcare work all create the same pattern: something tweaks, you push through the week, and by Monday it owns you. That's when a work injury chiropractor in Lenexa can matter more than people expect.

Meylor Chiropractic treats work-related injuries regularly. Here's what to jot down after it happens, what the first visit covers with Dr. Meylor, how workers' comp and insurance usually fit, and how evening appointments fit real schedules.

## What to write down after a work injury

### The basics on your phone

Keep a simple note on your phone the day it happens. Date and approximate time. What you were doing, lifting, twisting, repetitive motion, a slip. Where you feel it and what it feels like: sharp, dull, numb, shooting. Whether you reported it to a supervisor. Any witnesses. What made it better or worse that day.

That note helps your care and helps workers' compensation paperwork stay accurate. Don't rely on memory two weeks later when the details blur.

### Optional extras that help later

If you can, take a quick photo of the area or the equipment involved when it's safe to do so. You're not building a legal case in the parking lot. You're giving future-you better information. If a supervisor filled out an incident form, keep a copy or ask how to get one.

## Common work injuries we see in Lenexa and Johnson County

Low-back strains from lifting or awkward bends. Neck and shoulder tension from repetitive overhead work or long screen days. Disc-related pain that started as "just a tweak." Extremity issues that travel with the spine complaint. Flare-ups stacked on top of an older injury.

Overuse and repetitive stress cause more work injuries than dramatic one-time accidents. A delivery driver who twists out of the van hundreds of times a week. A nurse who leans over beds all shift. A desk worker who never leaves a chair that doesn't fit. Early care beats waiting until you can't get out of the truck.

People also come in from Overland Park, Shawnee, and Olathe with the same patterns. The Lenexa office on W 87th Street Parkway is set up for that Johnson County commute reality.

## What the first visit with Dr. Meylor covers

### Exam and findings

Dr. Jade Meylor walks through a thorough exam and listens to how the injury happened. The first visit typically includes a detailed chiropractic exam, neurologic testing, posture scans, and digital X-rays when appropriate. From there he builds a custom plan based on your condition and goals, not a generic "six visits" script.

### How work injuries show up in care

Spine-related care, disc issues, and extremity support all show up in work-injury cases. Acupuncture can be part of the picture when it fits. Details are on our [work injury](/services/chiropractic/injuries/work-injury/) page. If your incident overlaps with a vehicle on the job, [auto injury relief](/services/auto-injury-relief/) may be relevant too.

You'll leave knowing what we found and what we recommend next. If workers' comp is involved, say so up front so the office can handle billing questions correctly. Guessing later creates headaches for everyone.


If your employer needs a work status note, ask at the visit. Clear paperwork early prevents a second round of phone tag while you're still sore.
## Workers' comp, insurance, and paperwork

Meylor Chiropractic works with work-injury cases regularly and accepts insurance in many situations. Call to confirm yours before you assume coverage.

### What to bring and what to ask

Bring your insurance card and any workers' comp claim details you already have. Ask the front desk what documentation they need from your employer or the carrier. If you reported the injury, have the approximate report date ready.

Useful questions when you call: Do you work with my workers' comp carrier? What should I bring to the first visit? Do you have an evening opening this week? Can I start with a free consultation if I'm not sure yet?

We can't promise how a claim will settle. We can examine you, explain findings, and help keep the care record clear. That clarity matters if the claim file grows later.

If you're paying privately while a claim is sorting itself out, ask how billing is handled so you're not surprised. Timing and paperwork differ by carrier. The front desk has seen most of those patterns before.

## Evening appointments and same-day openings

Work injuries don't wait for a convenient Thursday morning. Meylor Chiropractic keeps [evening appointments](/evening-appointments/) so care can fit around shifts. Same-day openings aren't guaranteed every hour, but the team tries when the schedule allows.

If you're hurting today, call (913) 227-0909 and ask about the soonest opening. You can also start with a [free consultation](/free-consultation/) or use [appointment](/appointment/) / [contact](/contact/) online.

## Who should come in vs. who needs urgent care first

Come in for musculoskeletal strains, spinal pain after a work incident, and the kind of tweak that gets worse with each shift. Same if an older work injury keeps flaring and never fully settles.

Go to emergency or urgent care first for a serious fall, head impact, chest pain, or if you can't bear weight. Chiropractic evaluation is appropriate once you're medically stable, not instead of emergency care.

## Common mistakes after a workplace injury

Not reporting it. Waiting a week because "it'll go away." Stretching aggressively into sharp pain. Returning to heavy lifting the next morning to prove you're fine. All of those make recovery longer.

Another mistake: only treating the sore spot and ignoring how you move at work. If the job still loads the same tissue the same way, the flare comes back. Ask about practical modifications you can discuss with your supervisor when that's appropriate.

Quiet stoicism helps nobody, not you, not your claim file, not the exam. If symptoms change after heavier days, say so. The plan can adjust.

## Local context: Lenexa work life and why injuries linger

Lenexa and the surrounding Johnson County suburbs run on logistics, offices, healthcare, and retail. That mix produces the same injury patterns: repetitive lifts, long sits, awkward reaches, and the "I'll finish the shift" mindset. Cooler fall mornings add stiff starts to the day. Longer outdoor jobs in warmer stretches add fatigue.

A work injury chiropractor in Lenexa isn't only for dramatic accidents. If your job keeps loading the same irritated tissue, rest on Saturday often isn't enough. That's when a real exam and a plan for the week ahead matter more than another heating pad.


## What "better" can look like after a work injury

Better might mean finishing a shift without counting the minutes until you can sit down. It might mean sleeping past 3 a.m. without that sharp roll-over wake-up. It might mean looking over your shoulder to merge without grabbing the headrest.

Progress isn't always linear. A heavier week at work can stir things up even when the exam findings were improving. Say something when that happens. Quiet toughness just stretches the timeline.

If your job has light-duty options, ask what movements to avoid for now and what the office can put in writing for your supervisor. Clear limits beat vague "take it easy" advice that nobody can follow on a busy floor.

Bring that work-status question to the first visit if your employer already asked for paperwork. Getting the note wording right once saves a week of back-and-forth while you're still trying to get through shifts.

## Visit Meylor Chiropractic in Lenexa

We're at 12980 W 87th St Pkwy, Lenexa, KS 66215. Call (913) 227-0909. Serving Lenexa residents since 2005. If a work injury is already limiting your shift, don't wait for it to become your whole month.

## FAQ

**Do you take workers' compensation?**
We work with work-injury cases regularly. Call the office with your claim details so we can confirm what we need before your visit. Bringing your note about how it happened helps too.

**Should I go to urgent care first?**
If you had a serious fall, head impact, chest pain, or can't bear weight, get emergency or urgent care first. For musculoskeletal strains and spinal pain after a work incident, chiropractic evaluation is often appropriate once you're medically stable.

**How soon should I see a work injury chiropractor in Lenexa?**
As soon as you can. Waiting while inflammation and compensation patterns set in usually makes recovery longer. Same-day and evening options exist when the schedule allows.

**What should I bring to the first visit?**
Your phone note about the incident, insurance or workers' comp info if you have it, and a list of symptoms in your own words. Comfortable clothes help with the exam.

**Can desk workers have "real" work injuries?**
Yes. Repetitive strain and postural stress count. You don't need a dramatic warehouse accident for the injury to be work-related or worth evaluating.

**Do you accept health insurance?**
Often yes, but call to confirm your plan. Bring your card and ask about workers' comp billing if a claim is already open.

title: Sitting More Now That It's Cold? Why Sciatica Flares in Winter and What a Lenexa Chiropractor Can Do
excerpt: More sitting at the desk, on the couch and in the car can flare sciatica once it gets cold. What helps and what your first visit at Meylor includes.
content:
**TL;DR**

- Once the weather turns cold, most of us sit more: longer days at the desk, more evenings on the couch, and more time in the car.
- Long stretches of sitting can irritate the low back and the sciatic nerve, which shows up as pain, tingling or numbness from the low back or buttock down the leg.
- Getting up every 30 to 45 minutes, setting up your chair and car seat well, and staying active indoors all help.
- At Meylor Chiropractic & Acupuncture, your first exam visit includes a health history review, a full chiropractic exam, and X-rays and neurologic assessments when they are needed. We have after-work appointments from 3:00 to 6:00 PM, Monday through Thursday.

Summer in Lenexa keeps people moving. There are evening walks, yard work and kids' games every weekend. Then November hits, the sun sets before dinner, and most of that movement turns into sitting. Sitting at a desk all day, then on the couch all evening, then in the car on the weekend.

If you've dealt with sciatica before, this is often when it comes back. Here is why, what you can do about it at home, and what to expect when you come see Dr. Jade Meylor.

## What Is Sciatica?

Sciatica is pain that follows the path of the sciatic nerve, from the low back through the buttock and down the back of the leg, sometimes into the foot. It can feel sharp, burning or achy, and it often comes with tingling, numbness or weakness in the leg.

The sciatic nerve is the longest nerve in the body. It starts in the lumbar spine and travels through the buttock and down the leg. When something puts pressure on it or irritates it, you feel it along that path.

Common causes include disc injuries and bulges that press on the nerve root, as well as spinal misalignments tied to posture, pregnancy or an injury. Many people feel it come on suddenly, like when they bend to pick something up, even though the problem has been building for a while.

## Why Does Sciatica Flare Up When It Gets Cold?

Sciatica tends to flare in colder months because most people sit more and move less. Long periods of sitting keep your hips bent and put steady load on the discs and joints of your low back. With less walking and activity to balance it out, an irritated area has more chances to flare.

### At the desk

Fall and winter often bring busier stretches at work, and fewer people take a walk at lunch when it's 35 degrees out. Eight hours in a chair with few breaks is hard on a back that is already sensitive.

### On the couch

Darker evenings mean more time on the couch. Slouching into soft cushions, sitting with one leg tucked under you, or lying propped on an armrest can all leave your low back and hips in awkward positions for hours.

### In the car

Holiday travel adds long drives, and cold mornings mean sitting in the car while it warms up. Driving keeps your right leg working the pedals while your hips stay bent. A wallet in your back pocket can tilt your pelvis the entire drive.

### Bracing against the cold

People tend to tense up when they're cold. Stiff muscles and quick, careful movements on icy steps can add strain to an already irritated low back.

## What Can I Do at Home to Keep Sciatica From Flaring?

You can't avoid sitting entirely, but you can change how you do it.

- **Get up every 30 to 45 minutes.** Stand, walk to refill your water, or do a lap of the office. Short breaks add up.
- **Set up your desk.** Keep your feet flat, your hips slightly higher than your knees, and your screen at eye level. Our post on [desk posture](/patients/blog/the-posture-trap-how-desk-jobs-are-affecting-your-spine/) has more ideas.
- **Choose firmer seats at home.** A firm chair is often easier on sciatica than a deep, soft couch.
- **Empty your back pockets** before you drive or sit for a long time.
- **Stay active indoors.** Walking at a mall, a treadmill or a short routine at home keeps you moving when it's too cold outside.
- **Warm up before you shovel or lift.** Move around for a few minutes first, bend at the hips and knees, and keep loads close to your body.

If your pain keeps returning, or it starts to spread further down the leg, it is time to get it checked.

## How Can a Sciatica Chiropractor in Lenexa Help?

A chiropractor helps sciatica by finding what is irritating the nerve and treating that cause, rather than only the pain. At Meylor Chiropractic & Acupuncture, Dr. Meylor starts with a full evaluation, then builds a plan that usually includes gentle adjustments to help your spine move and line up the way it should.

How quickly you respond depends on the condition of the disc or joints involved and how long the problem has been going on. Our [sciatica treatment page](/services/chiropractic/spine-care/sciatica/) explains our approach in more detail, and if a disc is involved, our [disc injury page](/services/chiropractic/injuries/disc-injury/) covers that too.

Our team also offers [acupuncture](/services/acupuncture/), and some patients use it alongside chiropractic care. Dr. Meylor will tell you if he thinks it fits your plan.

One of our patients, Daniel, came to us on a doctor's referral with an inflamed sciatic nerve. In his Google review, he wrote that the rehab process was slow and took months, but that the small daily improvements helped him build other healthy habits along the way. Recovery looks different for everyone, and we will be honest with you about what to expect.

## What Does the First Visit Include?

Your first visit is about finding the cause before anyone starts treatment. Here is how it works.

### Start with a free consultation if you want

If you'd like to meet Dr. Meylor before committing to anything, start with our [free consultation](/free-consultation/). It's a one-on-one conversation with Dr. Jade Meylor that includes a review of your health history and concerns, an overview of chiropractic and acupuncture options, and answers to your questions about treatment, insurance or pricing. The consultation does not include exams, X-rays or treatment. If you need further evaluation, we'll tell you the costs and options before we go ahead.

### The comprehensive exam visit

At your comprehensive visit, we review your health history, do a full chiropractic examination, and perform any necessary X-rays and neurologic assessments. For sciatica, the goal is to figure out which structures are involved and what is irritating the nerve. Dr. Meylor then talks through what he found and builds a personalized care plan for you.

### Starting care

Once you have a plan, care usually begins with regular chiropractic adjustments and the holistic care that fits your situation.

## Who Is Dr. Jade Meylor?

Dr. Jade Meylor, D.C., FSBT, is a Sioux City, Iowa native who earned his Doctor of Chiropractic from Palmer College of Chiropractic in Davenport, Iowa. He has continued his training through postgraduate programs, including acupuncture and sports injury seminars, and is licensed in both Kansas and Missouri. Chiropractic runs in his family, with over 40 chiropractors in his extended family. Meylor Chiropractic has served Lenexa since 2005.

## Do You Take Insurance, and What Does It Cost?

Yes, we accept insurance. Call us to confirm your plan. Our team will be clear about pricing so you know what to expect before you're in the chair, and you can ask about insurance or pricing during your free consultation. You can also review our [Good Faith Estimate](/good-faith-estimate/) information.

## Can I Get an Evening Appointment?

Yes. We keep an afternoon-into-evening block from 3:00 to 6:00 PM, Monday through Thursday, so you can come in after work or school without taking time off. We also hold same-day openings every day we're open, and walk-ins are welcome. Learn more about our [evening appointments](/evening-appointments/).

## When Should Sciatica Be Checked Right Away?

Some symptoms need emergency care, not a chiropractic visit. Go to the ER if you have loss of bowel or bladder control, numbness in the groin or inner thighs, leg weakness that is getting worse quickly, or severe pain after a fall or car accident.

Long periods of sitting can irritate the low back and add pressure on the discs, which can aggravate sciatica, especially if you already have a disc or alignment problem. Regular movement breaks help.
